patterns.title: Vis-à-Vis Runner
patterns.description: Full three-block satin-damask runner: 682 working ends (684 physical threads, with doubled selvedges on shaft 16) and all 1,350 picks. The publisher's freely provided two-page lift plan completes the abbreviated threading printed on p.38; all continued brackets and single Safari/Pistachio picks are expanded. The loom-controlled selvedges are included.

patterns.title: Autumn Jewel Scarf
patterns.kind: Diversified plain weave and plain weave
patterns.description: Full 344-end threading with the three expanded diversified-plain-weave stripes and all 15 treadling repeats. Dark blue and purple fine warp ends are threaded randomly in the source; one dark tone represents that unspecified mixture. The variegated wool is approximated by its blue-green warp and pink-orange weft key colors.

patterns.title: Rainbow Sherbet Towels - Towel 1
patterns.description: Two-shaft hopsack design with the complete 462-end bracket expansion. Warp groups are held in threes and threaded in random color order in the published instructions; the catalog uses a repeatable ordering of those groups. Mock-plain-weave hems are included. Towel color versions follow the project's named palettes.

patterns.title: Dizzy Drones Honeycomb Pillows - Pillow 1
patterns.description: Complete 296-end honeycomb threading and this pillow's distinct thin-weft and denim-strip sequence, with every 4x bracket expanded. The 6-inch plain-weave sections at each end are represented by their two-pick repeat; repeat them to the specified length. Wet-finishing and denim-strip deflection create the honeycomb relief.

patterns.title: A Taste of Sonoma Scarf
patterns.description: Full 201-end barleycorn threading, 23 body repeats, three-pick and five-pick pattern groups, and the printed opening and closing color borders. Every tabby pick is explicit; the thicker Tawny wool pattern weft alternates with Tencel ground weft.

patterns.title: Blue Willow Towels
patterns.description: Complete 310-end color-and-weave threading with both 3x and 9x brackets expanded, and the 8x windowpane treadling repeat with its nested 2x groups. The two-inch hems are represented by one plain-weave cycle, to be repeated to length. All ground picks are explicit.

patterns.title: Corduroy Patch Pillow - front
patterns.description: Full 465-end six-shaft corduroy threading. The front contains every printed float-pattern repeat, with doubled Lavender Bright and Green Teal pattern yarns; cut the wool float columns after weaving to form pile. The back uses the separately printed four-pick plain-weave repeat, repeated for 23 1/4 inches. The drawdown represents interlacements before the pile is cut.

patterns.description: Full 465-end six-shaft corduroy threading. patterns.title: Taqueté All Day Tote
patterns.description: All three threading continuations are expanded. The publisher's complete 536-pick numeric lift plan supplies the exact shed and color on every pick, including red-leading blocks and separate cotton headers/footers. That official plan differs from the magazine diagram at its first pick of one block (pick 77) and some repeat extents, so the complete publisher plan is used. The skeleton tie-up's paired treadles are represented by their raised-shaft union; there is no inserted tabby.

patterns.title: Gilded Amethyst Scarf - advancing point
patterns.description: Complete 259-end threading with its continued 4x bracket and nested 2x group expanded. This is the separately labeled advancing point treadling from the printed draft. Gold pattern picks alternate with Amethyst tie-down picks, with the two tie-down sheds kept explicit. Repeat or combine these motifs as described in the project.

patterns.title: Mod Block Towels - Towel 1
patterns.description: Complete 576-end, four-block threading and the publisher's 1,524-pick standard treadling. The five 252-pick pattern blocks and the 132-pick hem/border sections use this towel's published weft colors. The printed 8-treadle skeleton tie-up produces the same raised-shaft unions; the standard version is stored once. All tabby picks are explicit.

notes: Show Your Team Spirit (pp.22-24) uses finnweave hand pick-up; its ground-only draft and logo pick-up charts are omitted under the existing catalog policy.
From Jacquard to Rigid Heddle (pp.25-28) contains illustrative pickup designs, not a complete numeric project draft.
Yarn Lab (pp.72-75) shows eight photographed samples but supplies no numerical threading/tie-up/treadling, so those are not invented.
The 17 numeric examples in The Draft: What Is a Twill? (pp.33-35) are included separately.
Vis-à-Vis Runner uses the official freely accessible lift-plan supplement linked by the issue, https://handwovenmagazine.com/files/75077/1722288901-o-hara-hwf24-runner-lift-plan.pdf.

Mod Block Towels uses the official standard-treadling supplement, https://handwovenmagazine.com/files/75077/1722460285-hwfa24-kaestner-mod-block-towels-lift-plan.pdf; its digit 0 denotes treadle 10, not a shaft.
Length-only plain-weave borders on Blue Willow and Honeycomb are stored as their short repeat, to be woven to the specified inch measurement.
Rainbow Sherbet randomizes the color order within three-end groups. A deterministic permissible order is used; every printed color-group count and every numbered weft-color repeat is expanded.
The three subscriber-exclusive photo-only projects on p.77 require separate project downloads and are outside the supplied issue; their drafts are not reconstructed from photographs.
